solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Wriggle, as maiden taken by nobleman endlessly

indicators.note: without its end, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: SQUIRE, a country gentleman, loses its last letter
M = maiden, a cricket scoring abbreviation

explanation.surface: A young woman squirms as a lord leads her off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken by' puts the maiden after the nobleman. A maiden is an over with no runs in cricket, marked M on the scorecard.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs describe twisting the body about, and squirm adds the embarrassment the maiden might feel.

clue.text: Something that goes with status rocker once mentioned

blocks.note: a Teddy boy, a 1950s rock'n'roll fan

explanation.surface: An old rocker cited as part of the establishment.
explanation.walkthrough: Teds were British 1950s youths in Edwardian-style suits who loved rock'n'roll, hence 'rocker once'. 'Status' is not a position here but the first half of a Latin phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of cited: a figure quoted in a report is one mentioned there.

clue.text: International regrets about revolutionary soldier in plots

explanation.surface: Remorse at an international level over a rebel fighter caught up in conspiracies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary soldier' suggests a guerrilla, but it only means the GI turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, both plural nouns for secret schemes against someone, as in court intrigues.

clue.text: Brilliant burner gives a nasty singe for mother to cover up

indicators.note: to cover something up is to put a layer over it on all sides

explanation.surface: A fierce flame singes someone, and mother has to hide the damage.
explanation.walkthrough: The burner is not a stove or a fire but a metal that burns with a dazzling white light.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnesium burns with an intensely bright white flame, used in flares and old camera flashes.

clue.text: Crystalline material found by fellow falling over in pit

explanation.surface: A miner who tumbles into a shaft discovers a crystal seam.
explanation.walkthrough: Melamine is best known as a hard plastic for tableware, but the compound itself is crystalline.
explanation.definitionFit: Melamine is a white crystalline compound used to make resins.

clue.text: Instrument making no sound needs to get fixed inside

indicators.note: the repair is done on the inside of the instrument

blocks.note: to set = to become fixed, as glue or jelly does

explanation.surface: A silent instrument needs repair work inside.
explanation.walkthrough: An instrument 'making no sound' sounds like a broken one, but it just gives MUTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A musette is a small bagpipe, popular in 17th- and 18th-century France.

clue.text: Manchester United could obviously lose – reverse starts with substitute

indicators.note: take the first letter of each word

blocks.note: first letters of the five words

explanation.surface: A football pundit says Manchester United may lose, so bring on a substitute.
explanation.walkthrough: The football picture makes 'substitute' look like a player coming off the bench; it is a stand-in doctor or cleric.
explanation.definitionFit: A locum is someone standing in temporarily for a doctor or priest.

clue.text: Bread dull, so we hear

indicators.note: what follows is by sound, not spelling

explanation.surface: Someone reports that the bread is boring.
explanation.walkthrough: Matt is the British spelling of matte, a non-shiny finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Matzo is the unleavened bread eaten at Passover.

clue.text: Rude teen must be disciplined, altered

indicators.note: the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A cheeky adolescent must be punished and changed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Altered' is the euphemism for a neutered pet, which gives the surface a darker second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A euphemism: vets and pet owners say altered for an animal that has been sterilised.

clue.text: Small houses can be prisons with excessive staying in

indicators.note: to stay in is to remain indoors

explanation.surface: A gloomy remark that a tiny home can feel like a jail if you're stuck in too long.
explanation.walkthrough: OTT (over the top) is common British shorthand for excessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by description: the word names a modest dwelling, typically rural, so small houses is its plain gloss.

clue.text: Fruit – it comes with mostly hard outer covering

indicators.note: all but the last letter of CRUST

explanation.surface: A description of fruit with a tough rind.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'hard outer covering' fits the fruit's own peel, which is the disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: Citrus fruit covers oranges, lemons, limes and their kin.

clue.text: Catty female totally heartless having row

indicators.note: the whole middle goes, leaving only the ends

blocks.note: FEMALE with all of EMAL removed

explanation.surface: A spiteful woman, completely cold, picking a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' tempts you to read a quarrel, matching catty; it is a line. Heartless usually drops one middle letter; 'totally' removes all four.
explanation.definitionFit: Feline means cat-like, which is what catty literally means.

clue.text: Book a singer

blocks.note: Henry Fielding's 1749 comic novel about a foundling
the Welsh pop singer of 'It's Not Unusual'

explanation.walkthrough: The slash just divides the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom Jones is Henry Fielding's 1749 novel and also the Welsh pop singer.

clue.text: A bit is missing from supporting beam

blocks.note: a joist is a floor beam; take IS out of its middle to leave JO and T

explanation.surface: A piece of a supporting beam has gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'is' in 'is missing' is also the letters to remove: the clue uses the word twice over.
explanation.definitionFit: A jot is a tiny amount, as in 'not a jot'.

clue.text: Country with marriage and civil partnership, say?

definitions.text: Country with marriage and civil partnership, say?

blocks.note: the surface wants a nation's laws; the answer is a nation's name

blocks.clueFragment: with marriage and civil partnership, say?
blocks.note: each is a state of being joined, a united state, and two of them make the plural

explanation.surface: A question about a nation that recognises both marriage and civil unions.
explanation.walkthrough: Marriage and civil partnership are both states of being united, so the country is literally 'united states'.
explanation.definitionFit: The United States is the country, and each union is a united state.

clue.text: Character in inferior position, it seems

explanation.surface: Someone with personality stuck in a lowly post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It seems' flags that the answer read as SUB STANCE is only a joke on the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of solid worth: a person of substance has real character.

clue.text: A famous swimmer grabbing kiss from great man

blocks.note: Leander swam the Hellespont nightly to see Hero
X = a kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A celebrity swimmer snatching a kiss from a VIP.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Great man' is not praise but a title: Alexander the Great.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the Macedonian conqueror carries 'the Great' as his title, so the clue borrows his epithet.

clue.text: Part of road giving entrance for traffic into naval base

indicators.note: the first letter, the way in

blocks.note: Faslane, the Royal Navy submarine base in Scotland

explanation.surface: Directions for traffic entering a navy base by road.
explanation.walkthrough: Faslane on the Clyde is the home of Britain's nuclear submarines.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by description: the overtaking lane of a motorway is one strip of the carriageway, so part of a road.

clue.text: Maybe dean’s gloomy journey in the churchyard?

explanation.surface: A clergyman's sombre walk among the graves.
explanation.walkthrough: The dance of death was a medieval image of skeletons leading the living to the grave, so the 'journey' ends in the churchyard.
explanation.definitionFit: A danse macabre is an allegorical procession of the dead, which suits a trip through a churchyard.

clue.text: The reverse of eager, mostly I’m alarmed!

explanation.surface: Far from keen, someone yelps in fright.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an exclamation, so it swaps for a cry of fright.
explanation.definitionFit: An interjection defined by the feeling behind it: the squeak of fright stands for a whole exclaimed sentence.

clue.text: Plant vehicle somewhere away from home

blocks.note: away = not at home, as in an away match

explanation.surface: An instruction to leave your car somewhere far from home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' reads as a verb, to park a car; it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Caraway is a plant grown for its aromatic seeds.

clue.text: See bird wag diving under water

blocks.note: a wag is a joker, a wit

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher points out a bird whose tail dips into the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wag' looks like a tail movement; it is a joker. To pass water is to urinate, hence PEE.
explanation.definitionFit: The peewit is the lapwing, named for its call.

clue.text: Martinet, persistent type giving learner detention

explanation.surface: A strict teacher keeps giving a pupil detention.
explanation.walkthrough: The school scene makes 'detention' a punishment; it just means holding L inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A martinet is a strict disciplinarian, a stickler for rules.

clue.text: Where land meets sea take it easy

blocks.note: the verb for moving along without effort, as a bike freewheels downhill

explanation.walkthrough: The slash divides the two definitions, a noun and a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The coast is the shoreline; to coast is to proceed with little effort.

clue.text: Coffee after appointed hour – little time for drinking

explanation.surface: A late coffee, with barely time to drink it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For drinking' looks like it belongs with the coffee; it is the container instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A latte is espresso with steamed milk.

clue.text: Bullet in drawer

blocks.note: a round that burns as it flies, leaving a visible trail
one who draws by tracing over an image

explanation.surface: A gun kept in a desk drawer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawer' is one who draws, not furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A tracer is a bullet that leaves a visible trail, and also someone who traces drawings.

clue.text: Scholar with old Bible in South Africa? Not all the Bible

blocks.note: the Authorised Version, the 1611 King James Bible
the New Testament, only part of it

explanation.surface: A learned man in South Africa with an antique Bible, but not the complete text.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bible is used twice: once as AV, the whole old translation, and once as NT, only one half of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym borrowed from French, where savant means knowing; both name someone of deep learning.

clue.text: Storm over? Chill out

blocks.note: a storm is a strong wind
down = over, finished, as in a wind that has died down

explanation.surface: Once the storm has passed, time to relax.
explanation.walkthrough: The weather picture makes 'chill' sound cold; it means relax.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: both phrasal verbs mean to unwind and relax after a busy spell.

clue.text: The early worms – tough

indicators.note: the letters wriggle into a new order

explanation.surface: The early bird's worms turn out chewy.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'the early bird catches the worm' makes 'worms' look like a noun; it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: like leather, something leathery is hard to chew or cut, the sense of tough meat.

clue.text: Time to admit bad person’s mistakes

indicators.note: to admit is also to let in, as a ticket admits you

blocks.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: It is time for a rogue to own up to his errors.
explanation.walkthrough: The ’s is short for 'is', joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Errata are listed errors in a printed work.
